briefs.label: Morning Brief
briefs.title: Tax-Relief Momentum in Lansing, Psychedelic Fast-Track in D.C.: Industry Turns a Corner
briefs.top: Michigan operators are finally seeing daylight on the 24% wholesale tax as a gubernatorial candidate courts industry cash and a Muskegon dispensary bets big on hospitality, even as JARS Cannabis expands into Arizona. Nationally, the FDA is clearing runway for psychedelic medicine while a federal court just protected the marijuana rescheduling gains operators have been waiting on.

local.text: JARS Cannabis buys its way into Arizona
local.detail: The Michigan-based chain is buying its way into a much bigger footprint out west, acquiring Sonoran Roots and its eight Ponderosa dispensaries to become Arizona's largest chain.
local.text_full: JARS Cannabis buys its way into Arizona — The Michigan-based chain announced a deal to acquire Sonoran Roots and its eight Ponderosa dispensaries, soon making JARS the largest dispensary chain in Arizona.

local.text: James courts cannabis cash with tax-repeal vow
local.text_full: James courts cannabis cash with tax-repeal vow — GOP gubernatorial nominee John James is proposing to repeal or sharply reduce the 24% wholesale tax, and a JARS-hosted fundraiser netted his campaign nearly $90,000.

local.text: State Supreme Court curbs weed-smell searches
local.text_full: State Supreme Court curbs weed-smell searches — Michigan cops can no longer search a car just because they think you have weed, per a new Michigan Supreme Court ruling that shields consumers and operators alike.

Muskegon dispensary-restaurant targets fall opening — Fields Cannary is targeting a fall launch for its retail dispensary, with a full-service restaurant to follow, pushing the hospitality format further than most Michigan stores.

local.text: Tax shortfall fuels bipartisan repeal push
local.text_full: Tax shortfall fuels bipartisan repeal push — The 24% wholesale tax generated only about $37 million in Q2 against a $105 million-per-quarter projection, and a GOP lawmaker's HB 6224 now aims to repeal it outright.

national.text: FDA hearing signals green light for psychedelics
national.text_full: FDA hearing signals green light for psychedelics — Jefferies analysts say the FDA's finalized trial guidance paired with its September 14 public hearing points to a more supportive regulatory environment for developers like Compass Pathways, Atai, Cybin and GH Research.

national.text: Compass Pathways nears first psilocybin approval
national.text_full: Compass Pathways nears first psilocybin approval — COMP360's NDA review is underway with final submission on track for Q4 2026, and Compass anticipates launch in the first half of 2027 pending FDA approval and DEA rescheduling.

national.text: Court rejects challenge to marijuana rescheduling
national.text_full: Court rejects challenge to marijuana rescheduling — A D.C. Circuit court left the medical marijuana Schedule III order in effect on Sept. 9, ruling that anti-rescheduling forces hadn't shown they'd win.

national.text: DEA itself now argues for Schedule III
national.text_full: DEA itself now argues for Schedule III — In its final post-hearing brief, the DEA told the court marijuana no longer meets the statutory criteria for Schedule I, a notable shift from the agency historically defending prohibition.

national.text: Vireo Growth expands footprint via Eaze buy
national.text_full: Vireo Growth expands footprint via Eaze buy — The multistate operator's acquisition of the delivery platform expands Vireo's operating footprint to 10 states with 166 dispensaries.
